extracted.intended_audience: NLP / machine learning researchers working on multimodal humor caption generation
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and evaluating models that generate funny captions for images (e.g., New Yorker cartoons) by combining visual understanding, humor reasoning, and creative imagination, using LLM-based multi-role frameworks. The page describes a theory-driven system (HOMER) with distinct roles for extracting script oppositions, expanding imaginative associations, and generating diverse captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor caption generation ... requiring visual understanding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models must correctly interpret the visual content of images (e.g., cartoons) as a prerequisite for producing contextually appropriate humorous captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor reasoning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems should reason about humor-relevant elements (incongruity, targets, scripts) rather than just producing generic text; aligns generation with humor-theoretic constructs (e.g., GTVH).

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative imagination
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models need to expand beyond literal image content to generate novel, imaginative associations that enable unexpected or surprising captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounding in key script oppositions (conflicting-script extractor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicting-script extractor that grounds humor in key script oppositions, forming the basis of caption generation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly identify script oppositions (contrasting scripts/concepts) as the core mechanism that produces humorous effects; use these oppositions to condition caption generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce funny and script-opposite captions
rubrics_metrics.description: To produce funny and script-opposite captions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target captions should leverage script-opposition to be perceived as humorous — i.e., create captions that invert or conflict with an expected script associated with the image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrieval-augmented hierarchical imaginator
rubrics_metrics.description: Retrieval-augmented hierarchical imaginator that identifies key humor targets and expands the creative space of them through diverse associations structured as imagination trees
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use retrieval from external data and organize associations hierarchically (imagination trees) to broaden the set of candidate humorous concepts and enrich creativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption generation conditioned on obtained knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Caption generator that produces funny and diverse captions conditioned on the obtained knowledge
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The caption generator should condition on extracted scripts and imaginative associations to produce multiple, diverse caption candidates that reflect the grounded humor reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of captions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation and generation should prioritize not only funniness but also diversity (varied humorous angles) to avoid repetitive or mode-collapsed outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretability
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing LLM-based approaches ... suffer from limited ... interpretability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer architectures and methods (e.g., multi-role decomposition) that make the generation process and humor-relevant decisions (script extraction, imagination paths) interpretable to humans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor-theory-driven design (GTVH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a novel LLM-based humor generation mechanism based on a fundamental humor theory, GTVH
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor model components and generation strategies in established humor theory (GTVH) to provide principled structure for extracting and exploiting humor-relevant features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical evaluation on benchmark datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive experiments on two New Yorker Cartoon benchmarking datasets show that HOMER outperforms state-of-the-art baselines and powerful LLM reasoning strategies on multi-modal humor captioning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure model performance on standard benchmark datasets (e.g., New Yorker cartoons), comparing against state-of-the-art baselines and LLM reasoning strategies; use empirical superiority on these datasets as evidence of effectiveness.
